# Design

How this app is built: its stack, layout and conventions.
Read it with `AGENTS.md`, which has the working rules and how the app is tested.

*The following is Angular's official best-practices rules file, included verbatim from
<https://angular.dev/assets/context/best-practices.md>. It is part of the Angular
architecture.*

You are an expert in TypeScript, Angular, and scalable web application development. You write functional, maintainable, performant, and accessible code following Angular and TypeScript best practices.

## TypeScript Best Practices

- Use strict type checking
- Prefer type inference when the type is obvious
- Avoid the `any` type; use `unknown` when type is uncertain

## Angular Best Practices

- Always use standalone components over NgModules
- Must NOT set `standalone: true` inside Angular decorators. It's the default in Angular v20+.
- Do NOT set `changeDetection: ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush` explicitly. `OnPush` is the default in Angular v22+.
- Use signals for state management
- Implement lazy loading for feature routes
- Do NOT use the `@HostBinding` and `@HostListener` decorators. Put host bindings inside the `host` object of the `@Component` or `@Directive` decorator instead
- Use `NgOptimizedImage` for all static images.
  - `NgOptimizedImage` does not work for inline base64 images.

## Accessibility Requirements

- It MUST pass all AXE checks.
- It MUST follow all WCAG AA minimums, including focus management, color contrast, and ARIA attributes.

### Components

- Keep components small and focused on a single responsibility
- Use `input()` and `output()` functions instead of decorators
- Use `model()` for two-way bound properties with `[(prop)]` syntax instead of pairing `input()` with `output()`
- Use `computed()` for derived state
- Use `linkedSignal()` for state derived from multiple reactive sources that must stay synchronized
- Prefer inline templates for small components
- Prefer Signal Forms (`@angular/forms/signals`) for new forms. They are stable in Angular v22+ and provide signal-based state, type-safe field access, and schema-based validation
- When not using Signal Forms, prefer Reactive forms instead of Template-driven ones
- Do NOT use `ngClass`, use `class` bindings instead
- Do NOT use `ngStyle`, use `style` bindings instead
- Do NOT import `CommonModule`, import only the directives and pipes the template uses, such as `AsyncPipe` or `DatePipe`
- When using external templates/styles, use paths relative to the component TS file.

## State Management

- Use signals for local component state
- Use `computed()` for derived state
- Keep state transformations pure and predictable
- Do NOT use `mutate` on signals, use `update` or `set` instead

## Templates

- Keep templates simple and avoid complex logic
- Use native control flow (`@if`, `@for`, `@switch`) instead of `*ngIf`, `*ngFor`, `*ngSwitch`
- Use the async pipe to handle observables
- Do not assume globals like (`new Date()`) are available.

## Services

- Design services around a single responsibility
- Use the `providedIn: 'root'` option for singleton services
- Prefer the `@Service` decorator over `@Injectable({providedIn: 'root'})` for new singleton services (Angular v22+)
- Use the `inject()` function instead of constructor injection

---

## Spring

This is a standard Spring Boot application, built with conventional Spring MVC
(`@RestController` request handling, a service layer, Spring Data / JPA persistence, and Bean
Validation). Follow ordinary Spring conventions and idioms throughout. Spring's reference
documentation is the guidance for the server: Spring Boot
<https://docs.spring.io/spring-boot/4.1/reference/> and Spring Framework
<https://docs.spring.io/spring-framework/reference/>.

=== sheet/AsOfFilter.java /** * The as-of view. A screen showing the sheet as of a date sends it on every request in the * {@value #HEADER} header. Such a request that only reads is answered from the sheet as it stood at * the end of that date (see {@link SheetHistory}), its today the date, in a transaction that is then * rolled back, so nothing it does is kept or audited; any other is refused (423) and changes nothing. * Without the header a request is served as it is, and once a change has been made the sheet is kept * as it now stands (taking or releasing a claim editor's lock is no change to keep). */ === sheet/SheetHistory.java /** * The sheet as it stood after each change, so it can be shown as of a date. After every change the * whole of the sheet's stored rows are kept (in {@code sheet_snapshot}) with the sheet's today then; * {@link #restore} puts the last one made on or before a date back in place of the sheet's rows, * its today the date, for the caller's transaction to read and then roll back. * *

The sheet's rows are found from the schema: every table with a {@code sheet_id}, and every * table without one that hangs off a person, claim, period or plan of the sheet. A table added later is * so kept without change here. */ === person/PersonMergeService.java /** * Merging a person into another on the sheet (a steward only). The merged person's claims move to * the other, keeping their numbers and dates, listed after the other's in the order they were added, * each keeping any figure a statement bound it to; their statements go to the other, listed before the * other's own (so the other's last statement stays theirs, or, having none, becomes the merged * person's); their name and aliases become aliases of the other; their patrons * are added to the other's (not the other themselves, no repeats), anyone naming them as patron names * the other instead (no repeats), and their pool memberships move to the other (shares added when the * other is already a member). Their holds, watchers and contact are dropped, and they leave the sheet. */ === person/PersonTransferService.java /** * Transferring a person to another sheet by id (a steward only). The person arrives there with * every grade they were given, their terms, contact and aliases, and their claims with their status, * dates, notes, tags, frozen figures and logs. Each claim that had a number takes the next number of * the other sheet, in the order the claims were opened (by the sheet's today when each was opened, * then by the order they were added). Figures a statement bound are kept, their statements go with * them (listed before those of a person they merge into, whose last statement stays theirs, or, having * none, becomes the transferred person's), and references are not carried. They leave this sheet entirely: patron links, pool * memberships, holds and watches are dropped. They and their claims arrive as new rows, so * this sheet's history (its as-of view) keeps its own. When the other sheet already has a person * with their name or an alias, they are merged into that person instead, as a merge does: their * claims are listed after that person's, their name and aliases become that person's aliases, and * their grades, terms and contact are dropped. */ === claim/ClaimPasteService.java /** * The paste box: lines of {@code name,amount,date,note}, each a DRAFT claim for the person of that * name or alias (compared without regard to case), added in order. The date may be blank (the sheet's today) * and the note may be absent or hold commas. A note ending in {@code " #"} gives the claim * that external reference, which is not part of the note; a reference repeated within the paste, or * already used on the sheet, refuses the whole paste. Every line is held to exactly the claim form's rules; * the paste is one change, so a refused line adds nothing and writes nothing. Blank lines are * skipped; a paste with no lines is refused. */ === quick/QuickAddService.java /** * Quick-add: a DRAFT claim of an amount, dated the sheet's today with an empty note, for the person * of a name or alias (compared without regard to case), adding the person with grade A first when the name is * not on the sheet. It is one change: a refused claim leaves no new person behind and writes nothing. */ === plan/PlanService.java /** * The people's plans: an amount, a start date, every N days (N at least 1) or monthly on a day of * the month (1 to 31), and an end date not before the start, added from the person's row. Generating goes through every plan on the sheet * in the order they were added and, for each plan date (the start, then every N days; or that day in every month from the start's month, on the month's * last day when it is shorter, dates before the start left out) up to the * end and the sheet's today that the plan has made no claim for yet, adds a DRAFT claim with the * plan's amount, dated that day with an empty note, by the claim form's rules: a date the form * refuses is skipped, and tried again on the next generate. */ === pool/PoolService.java /** * The sheet's pools: each a name, at most once on the sheet, and its members, each a person on the * sheet at most once per pool with a share percent (two decimals, above 0.00 and at most 100.00). * A pool's total adds up its members' shares, a retired member's (one with a retirement date set, * whatever the date) included as given; the pool is balanced when the total is exactly 100.00. *

* With a pot set on the sheet, each member of a balanced pool has a cut: the pot times their share * divided by 100, rounded half to even to two decimals. The remainder, the * pot less the cuts added up, goes to the member with the smallest non-zero cut (the latest added * on a tie; a member with no cut gets none, and a pool with no non-zero cut gives it to the last * member with a share), so the cuts total exactly the pot. An unbalanced pool, or no pot, has no cuts. *

* A retired person, and a person with a hold in force on the sheet's today (one whose dates include * today), has a cut of 0.00 in every pool, and their share is spread over the members left with a * cut: each of those cuts the pot times their share divided by the shares of the members with a cut * added up, half to even, the remainder as above (all 0.00 when no member is left with a cut). A * pool whose every member within their dates is retired shows no cuts. The pool's total share and * balance are unchanged by a hold or a retirement. *

* A member may instead be another pool, with a share like a person's. A pool is a member of at most * one pool, never contains itself through any chain, and a chain of pools is at most three deep. A * pool that is a member of another has no pot of its own: its pot is its cut in the pool above (so * an unbalanced pool above, or none, leaves it with no cuts). The sheet's pot is the pot of a pool * that is a member of none. *

* A membership may carry a from-date and a to-date (both inclusive, either optional; a to-date * before the from-date is refused). A member whose dates do not include the sheet's today is left * out entirely: not in the total share, not in the balance, and with no cut (blank). */ === sheet/SheetCloneService.java /** * Cloning a sheet to another id that was never used (a steward only). The clone gets the sheet's * today, settings, roles, rates, holidays, void reasons, templates, people (grades, terms, contacts, * aliases, tags, holds, retirements, patrons), pools, periods (all open) and claims with their * status, frozen figures, dates, notes and logs. Each claim that had a number is numbered afresh by * the clone's own numbering, in the order the claims were opened (by the sheet's today when each was * opened, then by the order they were added to the clone: by person in list order, each person's in * the order they were listed). Statements are not copied, so no figure is bound by one; nor are * watches, delegations or the sheet's history. * *

Rows are copied column by column as the schema has them, so a column added later is carried * without change here; only the columns that need another value are named. */ === setting/SettingService.java /** * The sheet's settings: its clerk limit (none: no limit) and its floor, the least a claim's live due * can be, and its terms, the days after its date a claim is due by, and its late percent, what an * overdue claim gains of its figure for every full 30 days overdue. Changing the floor or the late * percent moves the figures, so the figures that move are recorded. Its policy date (none: * the sheet's today) decides how a claim's live figures round (see {@link Rounding}), so changing it * records the figures that move too. Its period-numbering-from date (none: off) decides how a claim * opened is numbered: on or after it, within its period (see {@link SheetService#nextClaimNumber}). * Its cap (none: no cap) is the most a person's due-total can be, so changing it records the * figures that move too. A grade may have its own terms; a grade without uses the sheet's terms. A claim's due-by is fixed * when it is created, so changing any terms moves no claim's due-by. A grade may have grace days (none: no grace): a * claim whose person's grade on its date has grace days on that date is overdue only once its due-by plus them is * before the sheet's today, and its late charge counts its 30-day boundaries from there (see * {@link Sheet#lateFrom}); its due-by is unchanged. Changing a grade's grace days moves the figures, so the figures * that move are recorded. *

* The settings that carry a figure (the floor, the late percent, the terms, a grade's own terms, * a grade's grace days, the clerk limit, the cap, the proof threshold, a grade's own proof threshold and the note threshold) are dated: each value is recorded from a from-date (the sheet's * today when none is given). A claim's floor, late percent and terms are those in force on its * date, as is its proof threshold (its person's grade's own in force then when it has one, else the sheet's; see {@link Sheet#proofThresholdFor}) and its note threshold (see {@link Sheet#noteThresholdOn}); the clerk limit and the cap are those in force on the sheet's today (see {@link Sheet}). * The policy date and the period-numbering-from date are not dated. Nor is the permission matrix: * for each of open, settle, void, reassign, close and reopen, the roles that may take it (blank: the * standing rule, see {@link Sheet#permits}), recorded under the key {@code perm-}. Nor are * the grace days (none: off): when the sheet's today changes, every open period whose to-date plus * the grace days is before the new today is closed (see {@link SheetService#setToday}). Nor is the * entry date (none: off): while set, it is the default date of a new claim in place of the sheet's today. * Nor is the pot (none: no pot), shared out over each balanced pool's members as their cuts (see * {@link net.officefloor.hq.app.pool.PoolService}). Nor is the parent (none: no parent), a sheet that has * been loaded, never the sheet itself nor one that has it as an ancestor: a grade with no rate in force on a date * here takes its parent's, then the parent's parent's, up to three levels up (see {@link RateChain}), so changing it * records the figures that move too. Nor is the alert threshold (none: off): a change whose figures * lift a person's due-total above it records an ALERT (see {@link RollupService#recordChanges}); changing * it moves no figures. */

- **Settle or approve** fixes the charged due as it stands on today into `settledDue`. A steward can **re-settle**, which fixes it again at today's live figure as if the claim were open and unbound.

- **Clerk limit:** a clerk settling a claim whose figure is above the clerk limit makes it PENDING instead.
- **Proofs:** a claim above the proof threshold (the grade's own, else the sheet's) cannot be settled or approved without at least one proof.
- **Notes:** a claim above the note threshold cannot be opened with an empty note.
- **Period cap:** a period's `claimCap` limits each person's OPEN/PENDING claims in it.

- **A soft-closed period** only marks new claims as late entries.

- Deferring takes a claim out of every total until its deferral date; a deferred claim can't be settled.
- A DELETED claim can be restored only on the same sheet-today it was deleted.

- **Person import:** a line whose name matches an existing person edits them (grade from today, terms and contact only if given). Any other line adds a person. It is all-or-nothing and refuses repeated names or contacts within the import.
- **Claim paste:** adds DRAFT claims, all-or-nothing. A `#ref` at the end of a note sets the claim's reference.
- **Hold:** removes the person's OPEN and PENDING claims dated within it from every total — their own, the sheet's and the periods' — but not stated or settled claims. It also gives the person a cut of 0 in pools.
